disclaimer: Facts as written; not advice; doctors decide.
summary: Synthetic example (fictional person). Four items: a label note on how dutasteride affects PSA readings, a label warning on tamsulosin and orthostasis next to a family-reported dizziness, and a guideline practice point on kidney testing next to a single recorded eGFR with no urine albumin result. Three questions for the treating doctors. No red flags in the recorded window.

items.statement: The current dutasteride label states that dutasteride reduces serum PSA by approximately 50% within 3 to 6 months, and that an isolated PSA in a man treated for 3 months or more is compared with untreated reference values only after doubling. The recorded PSA (10-Sep-2026) was printed against an untreated reference range; dutasteride is recorded as strip-seen since 03-Feb-2026.

applicability.notes: US label used as a proxy; the Indian package insert could not be fetched. The label statement covers men on dutasteride generally.

citations.title: AVODART (dutasteride) capsules, prescribing information
citations.quote: To interpret an isolated PSA value in a man treated with AVODART for 3 months or more, the PSA value should be doubled for comparison with normal values in untreated men.

items.statement: The current tamsulosin label lists orthostasis (postural hypotension, dizziness and vertigo) as reported more often with tamsulosin than with placebo. A family-reported episode of dizziness on standing is recorded on 05-Oct-2026; tamsulosin is recorded as strip-seen.

applicability.notes: Generic US label used as a proxy. The dizziness is family-reported, with no recorded blood pressure at the time; other recorded medicines may also be relevant and are for the doctor to weigh.

citations.title: Tamsulosin hydrochloride capsules, prescribing information
citations.quote: The signs and symptoms of orthostasis (postural hypotension, dizziness, and vertigo) were detected more frequently in tamsulosin hydrochloride capsule-treated patients than in placebo recipients.

items.statement: KDIGO 2024 advises testing people at risk for and with CKD using both urine albumin and GFR (practice point, ungraded). The records hold one eGFR (52, 12-Oct-2026, printed flag L) and a doctor-written type 2 diabetes; no urine albumin result is recorded.

applicability.notes: A single value; the printed eGFR equation is not stated on the report. Practice points are expert guidance, not graded evidence.

citations.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
citations.quote: Test people at risk for and with chronic kidney disease (CKD) using both urine albumin measurement and assessment of glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

items.statement: secondary: reports AUA BPH guideline recommendation. A StatPearls chapter on BPH states, in its own words, that PSA testing may be offered to men with lower urinary tract symptoms when it would change management. A doctor-written BPH is recorded; the AUA guideline itself is linked for the urologist at its BPH guideline page (section on diagnostic evaluation) and is not quoted here.

applicability.notes: Secondary reference text; its wording is not the AUA's. Synthetic: the quoted sentence is a placeholder for what the real chapter says.

citations.title: AUA guideline on management of BPH
citations.locator: Diagnostic evaluation section (recommendation number to be read by the clinician)

citations.title: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (StatPearls)
citations.quote: Synthetic placeholder sentence standing in for a verbatim StatPearls quote on PSA testing in men with lower urinary tract symptoms.

questions.text: Treating urologist: the 10-Sep-2026 PSA was recorded while dutasteride is on the medicine list (rx-001). How should this result be read, and when is the next PSA due?
Treating urologist: dizziness on standing was reported at home on 05-Oct-2026, and the tamsulosin label lists orthostasis (rx-002). Is this worth checking, for example with a standing blood pressure?
Treating physician: one eGFR of 52 is recorded and no urine albumin result (rx-003). Is a repeat kidney test or a urine albumin-creatinine ratio due?

search_log.notes: KDIGO 2024 has no PubMed abstract; quote taken from the guideline PDF at kdigo.org (practice point 1.1.1.1)

triggers: new eGFR or urine albumin result

read_checklist.title: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)

limitations: Synthetic example: the person, KB ids and dates are fictional; the citations are real.
Indian package inserts were not available; US labels used as proxies.
Not a systematic review; no literature pass was needed because the label and guideline passes answered each topic.
rx-004 is a synthetic illustration of the secondary-source pattern: its quote is a placeholder, not real StatPearls text.
